SOURCE: "Mathematical Capabilities of ChatGPT", Simon Frieder, Luca Pinchetti, Alexis Chevalier, Ryan-Rhys Griffiths, Tommaso Salvatori, Thomas Lukasiewicz, Philipp Christian Petersen, Julius Berner. No venue is printed; the only stamp is "arXiv:2301.13867v2 [cs.LG] 20 Jul 2023", so cite as a preprint (2023). First-author affiliations as printed: "Department of Computer Science, University of Oxford, Oxford, UK" and "Faculty of Mathematics, University of Vienna, Vienna, Austria".
File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/08-eval/sources/frieder-2023-mathematical-capabilities-chatgpt.pdf

COVERAGE: 37 of 37 pages, 131,436 of 131,436 chars. Read in full: body (pp. 1-9), appendices A-D.5 (pp. 13-24), datasheet E (pp. 32-37). Skimmed: references (pp. 10-12) and the D.6 best-3/worst-3 raw examples (pp. 25-31), which hold no results.

CLAIMS
- claim: GHOSTS is 709 prompts in six subdatasets (17 files), giving 1,636 expert ratings.
  number: 709; 1636
  setup: (709+24 prompt-engineered) x 2 ChatGPT versions + 170 GPT-4
  quote: "in total(709+24)×2+170 = 1636 outputs and evaluations have been carried out"
  where: p32 (Q6); Table 1 p5
- claim: The authors wrote and graded everything themselves; there was no crowdsourcing.
  number: none
  setup: raters hold master's to professor-level positions; harder prompts went to more senior people
  quote: "The evaluation was carried out by a subset of the authors of this paper who have substantial mathematical expertise, ranging from master's degrees in mathematics to postdoc-level and professor-level positions [...] No third parties were involved."
  where: pp17-18 (B.6)
- claim: Sources are textbook exercises (Rudin, Munkres, Durrett; Engel for olympiad), math.stackexchange and Axler/Rudin proofs with parts deleted, random samples of MATH (Hendrycks) and of Lample & Charton integrals (converted by hand from Polish notation), and expert-written search-style prompts.
  number: sizes per subdataset from Table 1: Grad-Text 130, Holes-in-Proofs 162, Olympiad 101 (+24), Symbolic-Integration 100, MATH 138, Search-Engine-Aspects 78
  where: pp4-5
- claim: Free-text expert grading is argued for because proofs have no short checkable answer.
  quote: "unlike in the case of the MATH dataset by [11] (see Section 2), the answer to most of our prompts cannot be condensed into a few tokens (such as a number or a function), e.g., when the answer is a mathematical proof."
  where: p6; p32 Q1 adds "going beyond math problems that are yes-no rated"
- claim: Rating scale 1-5: 1 query not understood, 2 understood but entirely wrong, 3 partially correct, 4 mostly correct, 5 completely correct. Error codes e1 (missing information), e2 (a few wrong/vague statements), e3 (many), e4 (wrong computation), e5_1 to e5_5 (logic: unrelated statements, missing step, missed edge case, unsupported inference, circular), e6 (rules not respected). Warning codes w1 withholding, w2 rambling, w3 hallucinating, w4 weird, w5 notation changed. An error code is mandatory for ratings 2-4 and barred at 5.
  quote: "If a ratingr with 1 < r < 5 has been given, then an error code is mandatory"
  where: pp16-17 (B.4)
- claim: Rating agreement was not measured; the only check was a small spot review.
  number: fewer than 10 per dataset
  quote: "Random samples (< 10) were drawn from each dataset, and a second assessor reviewed the rating. If deemed problematic, the original assessors were asked to re-evaluate."
  where: p17 (B.5)
- claim: Headline means: ChatGPT 9-Jan 3.20 (SD 1.23) and 30-Jan 3.29 (SD 1.28) on GHOSTS; GPT-4 4.15 (SD 1.12) on miniGHOSTS only. Pass line is 3.5.
  quote: "GPT-4, which achieved a substantially higher average rating of4.15 (standard deviation: 1.12)"
  where: p7
- claim: By subdataset, 9-Jan: Symbolic-Integration 2.51 (GPT-4 3.50 on its 10-item subset); MATH perfect score on 29% (GPT-4 70%); Olympiad worst, with 75% rated 2 and no 5s; Reverse Definition Retrieval best at 4.30 (SD 1.14).
  quote: "75% of the scores are2 because the answer does not show any promise. No rating of 5 was awarded"
  where: pp7, 20. Other per-file means exist only as bars in Figure 1.
- claim: The same aggregate hid item-level churn between the two ChatGPT versions.
  quote: "roughly the same amount of outputs that received grade 4, yet less than half of the prompts were the same between model changes"
  where: p7
- claim: miniGHOSTS takes 10 prompts from each of 17 files (170), chosen to match each file's mean and SD of ratings on the 30-Jan version, then hand-picked for mathematical diversity.
  quote: "computing all subsets of10 prompts having approximately the same mean rating and standard deviation as the original file from GHOSTS, rated on the 30-January-2023 version of ChatGPT. A manual inspection of these subsets [...] then led to the final selection"
  where: p34 (Q24)
- claim: Prompt engineering (step-by-step, "Prove that") on about 20% of Olympiad items cut e2-e4 errors, raised e5 logic errors, and barely moved the mean.
  where: p19

LIMITS
- Conceded: human error; checks "not exhaustive"; too small for fine-tuning; no dev/test split ("Not applicable").
- Not shown: any agreement statistic; whether raters were blind to model version; that miniGHOSTS tracks GHOSTS for any model other than the one it was fitted on. GPT-4 was never run on the full set, so its 4.15 is not on the same items as 3.20/3.29 (Figure 2 does compare all three on miniGHOSTS).
- Contamination is argued, not tested: Polish-notation encoding, terse book solutions, dialogue-style prompts. Grad-Text comes from standard textbooks.
- One sample per prompt through the web GUI with unknown temperature; the 130 Grad-Text prompts are withheld for copyright (references only).
- Dated: early-2023 models.

BUILDS ON: Hendrycks et al. 2021 (MATH); Lample and Charton 2019 (symbolic integration); Welleck et al. 2021/2022 (NaturalProofs, NaturalProver human evaluation schema); Ling et al. 2017 (AQuA-RAT JSON format); Gebru et al. 2021 (Datasheets for Datasets).

CODE: none worth keeping. The row schema keys (p6) are prompt, output, rating, errorcodes, warningcodes, comment, msc, ref, confidence, timestamp.

FIGURES: Figure 1, p8, "Average rating for each file in each subdataset (bold) of GHOSTS on the 9-January-2023 and the 30-January-2023 versions of ChatGPT and for miniGHOSTS on GPT-4", with 95% CIs and the 3.5 pass line. It is the only place the per-file results appear, and it shows scores falling with difficulty.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions. JSON listings are extracted letter-spaced, and Figure 5's count matrix lost its column alignment, so I report no per-code counts from it beyond those stated in prose. Internal inconsistencies: Olympiad is "one hundred exercises" in text but 101 in Table 1; Section 3 says the subset has "the same" mean and SD, the datasheet says "approximately"; the Figure 6 caption says "right" twice.
